title: Review of c46's hunting ecology (fresh seed 7 at 256^2, predator-free twin, fuel fork at 128^2): S, I, X, predator D and prey E reproduce (21 predator persistent splits, generation 2; prey 54 -> 5 -> 56 against a static 85-body twin; prey 15 -> 0 within 500 t of the fuel cut), but the prey divide once (twin 27) and the predator's E is by construction, so no one kind shows I, D and a dynamical E together; one predator-prey cycle, not several; Weak
summary: Fresh-seed labkit re-run of the claimed world at 256^2 (seed 7, t=12000, --lineage-k 5), its predator-free twin (pred_on 0) and c46's drive.py fuel fork at 128^2 (fork_t 6000, seed 7, with the fed run alongside). Prey condensates form from noise; predator droplets appear on them after t=2000, eat the prey from 54 to 5 bodies by t~3000, then fall back while the prey regrow to 56 by t~5000; after that both decline slowly (prey 24-27, predators 27-44 at t 8000-12000), so this seed shows one lagged crash and recovery rather than repeated cycles. Predators: 21 persistent splits (generation 2, merge/split 0.10); the strict strip test (c46's splits3.py) finds 17 predator splits at a minimum area of 8 px, 11 away from prey (2 at 30 px; the claim's area threshold is not stated), and strict_pred_A8.png shows rods and Y-shapes pinching into separate droplets. Prey: 1 persistent split (strict test 1) against 27 in the twin (strict 25), whose prey grow from 46 to 85 bodies without cycling: X reproduces, D for prey does not. Fuel fork: prey 15 -> 3 -> 0 by t=6500 with prey material conserved (mean 0.225 -> 0.218), the fed run keeps 8-15; predators persist on dissolved prey (13-14).

verdicts.limitation: The capabilities split across kinds: predators show I and D, with E by construction (they are made only from prey material) and they survive the fuel cut on dissolved prey; prey show the dynamical E but almost never divide (new prey nucleate from the refilled bath). One seed at 256^2; the strict split count depends on the minimum area (17 at 8 px, 2 at 30 px); the fork was run at 128^2 with drive.py counts, as in the claim.
